assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a textbook problem of biological energy and electron/proton transfer chemistry: how an Fe-Mo-cofactor reduces N2 using coupled ATP-driven electron delivery. Crystal structures of the MoFe and Fe proteins, the interstitial carbide of the cofactor, and the Lowe-Thorneley-style kinetic framework with spectroscopic trapping of intermediates give a physically stated mechanism of high lasting importance, with industrial and ecological reach.
assessment.attribution: Structure is credited chiefly to Rees (first structures and later cofactor work) and Einsle (atomic-resolution cofactor with central carbide); Seefeldt and Dean/Ribbe contributed mechanism and cofactor biosynthesis. Three-laureate fit is plausible but the split between structure and mechanism people is contestable and Dean/Ribbe are a real alternative.
assessment.maturity: Structures and carbide assignment are independently confirmed; recent cryo-EM of turnover states and N2-bound states are strengthening the mechanism but the catalytic cycle is still not fully resolved. Recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the field is judged as a line of work rather than one attributable discovery
Exact priority among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt
Unresolved N2 binding mode and which redox states of the cofactor bind substrate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins, probed with photo-triggered ruthenium-modified proteins, quantified distance and driving-force dependence and showed how the polypeptide medium tunes tunnelling. It anchors the physical understanding of respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, which I regard as central to biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are a compact, clean pair with a long joint record; the theoretical foundation (Marcus, Hopfield, Beratan-Onuchic) lies outside the credited names and was already partly recognised by earlier prizes, which affects how much remains for a new award.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation (Dutton, Moser, Page, others) and stable interpretation; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the theoretical contribution of the Marcus prize
Whether the committee sees this as a bioinorganic method or as a general principle of protein function
Declared affinity: this is close to my own field

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allowed structures from micro-crystals before radiation damage and made time-resolved molecular movies of reactions in enzymes and photoreceptors possible. It is a methodological breakthrough that makes mechanisms visible, which I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffraction-before-destruction concept and the first SFX demonstration; Fromme and Schlichting contributed biological sample delivery, crystals and early time-resolved work; Hajdu, a key originator, is deceased and not eligible. The three-name choice is debatable, with Spence and others outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Now broadly adopted with many independent facilities, and time-resolved results are being confirmed. The strongest biological payoffs are still accumulating, so timing is acceptable but not late.
uncertainties: Hajdu's deceased status and credit for the founding concept
Credit split between concept, sample delivery and facility development
Physics-versus-chemistry boundary of an X-ray source and method advance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical mode of pharmacology, hijacking E3 ligases to remove proteins. The concept is clear and original, with strong clinical momentum and a defined chemical mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli made structure-based VHL ligands and degrader design. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue story (Handa, Ito) is a separate decisive contribution that complicates a three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly validated across many labs and in clinical trials, but approved drugs are still lacking, so some may argue it is a few years early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose PROTAC and molecular-glue parts may require different recognition
Clinical maturity not yet demonstrated
Handa and Ito priority on cereblon not fitting within three

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, by fusing deaminases to Cas proteins. This is a conceptually clear chemical solution to precise genome editing with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the central inventor of cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors; Nishida and Kondo reported a parallel cytidine system. A single-laureate configuration is defensible but the contribution of the lead scientists is notable.
assessment.maturity: Early clinical use is emerging and independent validation is broad. The genome-editing area has already been recognised in 2020, which raises the bar on distinctiveness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize
Clinical durability and off-target profile still being established
Whether trainee contributions should be credited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensation by liquid-liquid phase separation reframed how cells organise biochemistry without membranes and brought physical-chemistry concepts of phase behaviour into cell biology. The impact is broad, though the quantitative link to mechanism in vivo is still maturing.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behaving as liquids; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work gave a quantitative biochemical basis. Pappu and Mittag contribute physical theory, so more than three people have credible claims.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited but contested for physiological relevance in some systems; interpretation is not yet fully stable and some claims are premature.
uncertainties: Physiological significance disputed for many proposed condensates
Credit among five or more plausible contributors
Whether this is more cell biology than chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer provides a unified physical description of concerted proton and electron movement, spanning theory, model systems and enzyme mechanism, and it underlies energy conversion in respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes. This is a mechanism-level concept with clear lasting value.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Nocera established experimental model systems and thermodynamic frameworks, Hammes-Schiffer formulated the theory, and Meyer contributed early electrochemical work. The inclusion of Meyer makes a clean three-name split difficult.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely confirmed, but the identification of a single discovery is harder; it is closer to a field than a single decisive finding.
uncertainties: Rests on a line of work rather than a single discovery
Close to my own research, so I may be biased
Priority between Meyer and the others

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods allowed structure and dynamics determination of larger proteins in solution, notably through TROSY-based and methyl-labelling approaches, and made time-dependent motion visible at atomic resolution. Impact on structural biochemistry is very large.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay each made major distinct contributions; Wagner and Palmer have credible claims. The 2002 Wüthrich prize recognised NMR structure determination, so the claim must rest on dynamics and large-system methods.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation; timing is not an issue but the novelty relative to the 2002 prize is.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 NMR prize
Large field with five named contributors
Competition from cryo-EM for structure determination
